Topic.label: Identifying equally likely outcomes and classical probability models

Question: A biased die is rolled. Can 1/6 be used as the probability of rolling a 6? Why?

Choices.A: Yes, because the die has 6 faces.
Choices.B: No, because the scores are not equally likely, so the equal-likelihood requirement is not satisfied.
Choices.C: Yes, because rolling a 6 is only 1 outcome.
Choices.D: No, because there are infinitely many outcomes.

Solution: The value 1/6 is calculated using \(P=m/n\), which requires all outcomes to be equally likely. When the die is biased, the scores are not equally likely, so 1/6 cannot be used directly.

Original.prompt: 抛一枚不均匀的骰子，能否用 1/6 作为出现 6 点的概率？为什么？

choices.text: 能，因为骰子有 6 个面
不能，因为各点数出现的可能性不相等，不满足等可能
能，因为 6 点只有一种结果
不能，因为结果有无限多种

Original.explanation: 1/6 是用 P=m/n 算得的，要求所有结果等可能。骰子不均匀时各点数的可能性不相等，不能直接用 1/6。
